metrics.name: num_perplexity_tokens
metrics.description: Average number of tokens in the predicted output (for language modeling, the input too).

metrics.name: num_bytes
metrics.description: Average number of bytes in the predicted output (for language modeling, the input too).

metrics.name: num_references
metrics.description: Number of references.

metrics.name: num_train_trials
metrics.description: Number of trials, where in each trial we choose an independent, random set of training instances.

metrics.name: estimated_num_tokens_cost
metrics.description: An estimate of the number of tokens (including prompt and output completions) needed to perform the request.

metrics.name: num_prompt_tokens
metrics.description: Number of tokens in the prompt.

metrics.name: num_prompt_characters
metrics.description: Number of characters in the prompt.

metrics.name: num_completion_tokens
metrics.description: Actual number of completion tokens (over all completions).

metrics.name: num_output_tokens
metrics.description: Actual number of output tokens.

metrics.name: max_num_output_tokens
metrics.description: Maximum number of output tokens (overestimate since we might stop earlier due to stop sequences).

metrics.name: num_requests
metrics.description: Number of distinct API requests.

metrics.name: num_instances
metrics.description: Number of evaluation instances.

metrics.name: num_train_instances
metrics.description: Number of training instances (e.g., in-context examples).

metrics.name: prompt_truncated
metrics.description: Fraction of instances where the prompt itself was truncated (implies that there were no in-context examples).

metrics.name: finish_reason_length
metrics.description: Fraction of instances where the the output was terminated because of the max tokens limit.

metrics.name: finish_reason_stop
metrics.description: Fraction of instances where the the output was terminated because of the stop sequences.

metrics.name: finish_reason_endoftext
metrics.description: Fraction of instances where the the output was terminated because the end of text token was generated.

metrics.name: finish_reason_unknown
metrics.description: Fraction of instances where the the output was terminated for unknown reasons.

metrics.name: num_completions
metrics.description: Number of completions.

metrics.name: predicted_index
metrics.description: Integer index of the reference (0, 1, ...) that was predicted by the model (for multiple-choice).

metrics.name: exact_match
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly.

metrics.name: quasi_exact_match
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference up to light processing.

metrics.name: prefix_exact_match
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches the prefix of a correct reference exactly.

metrics.name: quasi_prefix_exact_match
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches the prefix of a correct reference up to light processing.

metrics.name: exact_match@5
metrics.description: Fraction of instances where at least one predicted output among the top 5 matches a correct reference exactly.

metrics.name: quasi_exact_match@5
metrics.description: Fraction of instances where at least one predicted output among the top 5 matches a correct reference up to light processing.

metrics.name: prefix_exact_match@5
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output among the top 5 matches the prefix of a correct reference exactly.

metrics.name: quasi_prefix_exact_match@5
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output among the top 5 matches the prefix of a correct reference up to light processing.

metrics.name: logprob
metrics.description: Predicted output's average log probability (input's log prob for language modeling).

metrics.name: logprob_per_byte
metrics.description: Predicted output's average log probability normalized by the number of bytes.

metrics.name: bits_per_byte
metrics.description: Average number of bits per byte according to model probabilities.

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.description: Perplexity of the output completion (effective branching factor per output token).

metrics.name: rouge_1
metrics.description: Average ROUGE score [(Lin, 2004)](https://aclanthology.org/W04-1013/) based on 1-gram overlap.

metrics.name: rouge_2
metrics.description: Average ROUGE score [(Lin, 2004)](https://aclanthology.org/W04-1013/) based on 2-gram overlap.

metrics.name: rouge_l
metrics.description: Average ROUGE score [(Lin, 2004)](https://aclanthology.org/W04-1013/) based on longest common subsequence overlap.

metrics.name: bleu_1
metrics.description: Average BLEU score [(Papineni et al., 2002)](https://aclanthology.org/P02-1040/) based on 1-gram overlap.

metrics.name: bleu_4
metrics.description: Average BLEU score [(Papineni et al., 2002)](https://aclanthology.org/P02-1040/) based on 4-gram overlap.

metrics.name: f1_set_match
metrics.description: Average F1 score in terms of set overlap between the model predicted set and correct reference set.

metrics.name: f1_score
metrics.description: Average F1 score in terms of word overlap between the model output and correct reference.

metrics.name: classification_macro_f1
metrics.description: Population-level macro-averaged F1 score.

metrics.name: classification_micro_f1
metrics.description: Population-level micro-averaged F1 score.

metrics.name: absolute_value_difference
metrics.description: Average absolute difference between the model output (converted to a number) and the correct reference.

metrics.name: distance
metrics.description: Average gometric distance between the model output (as a point) and the correct reference (as a curve).

metrics.name: percent_valid
metrics.description: Fraction of valid model outputs (as a number).

metrics.name: NDCG@10
metrics.description: Normalized discounted cumulative gain at 10 in information retrieval.

metrics.name: RR@10
metrics.description: Mean reciprocal rank at 10 in information retrieval.

metrics.name: NDCG@20
metrics.description: Normalized discounted cumulative gain at 20 in information retrieval.

metrics.name: RR@20
metrics.description: Mean reciprocal rank at 20 in information retrieval.

metrics.name: math_equiv
metrics.description: Fraction of model outputs that are mathematically equivalent to the correct reference.

metrics.name: math_equiv_chain_of_thought
metrics.description: Fraction of model outputs that are mathematically equivalent to the correct reference when using chain-of-thought prompting.

metrics.name: exact_match_indicator
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly, ignoring text preceding the specified indicator (e.g., space).

metrics.name: final_number_exact_match
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly, ignoring text preceding the specified indicator.

metrics.name: exact_set_match
metrics.description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly as sets.

metrics.name: iou_set_match
metrics.description: Intersection over union in terms of set overlap between the model predicted set and correct reference set.

metrics.name: training_co2_cost
metrics.description: Estimate of the CO2 emissions from training the model.

metrics.name: training_energy_cost
metrics.description: Estimate of the amount of energy used to train the model.

metrics.name: inference_runtime
metrics.description: Average observed time to process a request to the model (via an API, and thus depends on particular deployment).

metrics.name: inference_idealized_runtime
metrics.description: Average time to process a request to the model based solely on the model architecture (using Megatron-LM).

metrics.name: inference_denoised_runtime
metrics.description: Average time to process a request to the model minus performance contention by using profiled runtimes from multiple trials of SyntheticEfficiencyScenario.

metrics.name: batch_size
metrics.description: For batch jobs, how many requests are in a batch.

metrics.name: ece_1_bin
metrics.description: The (absolute value) difference between the model's average confidence and accuracy (only computed for classification tasks).

metrics.name: max_prob
metrics.description: Model's average confidence in its prediction (only computed for classification tasks)

metrics.name: ece_10_bin
metrics.description: The average difference between the model's confidence and accuracy, averaged across 10 bins where each bin contains an equal number of points (only computed for classification tasks). Warning - not reliable for small datasets (e.g., with < 300 examples) because each bin will have very few examples.

metrics.name: platt_ece_1_bin
metrics.description: 1-bin ECE computed after applying Platt scaling to recalibrate the model's predicted probabilities.

metrics.name: platt_ece_10_bin
metrics.description: 10-bin ECE computed after applying Platt scaling to recalibrate the model's predicted probabilities.

metrics.name: platt_coef
metrics.description: Coefficient of the Platt scaling classifier (can compare this across tasks).

metrics.name: platt_intercept
metrics.description: Intercept of the Platt scaling classifier (can compare this across tasks).

metrics.name: selective_cov_acc_area
metrics.description: The area under the coverage-accuracy curve, a standard selective classification metric (only computed for classification tasks).

metrics.name: selective_acc@10
metrics.description: The accuracy for the 10% of predictions that the model is most confident on (only computed for classification tasks).

adapter.name: method
adapter.description: The high-level strategy for converting instances into a prompt for the language model.

adapter.name: global_prefix
adapter.description: The string that is prepended to the entire prompt.

adapter.name: global_suffix
adapter.description: The string that is appended to the entire prompt.

adapter.name: instructions
adapter.description: The description of the task that is included at the very beginning of the prompt.

adapter.name: input_prefix
adapter.description: The string that is included before each input (e.g., 'Question:').

adapter.name: input_suffix
adapter.description: The string that is included after each input (e.g., '\n').

adapter.name: reference_prefix
adapter.description: The string that is included before each reference (for multiple-choice questions).

adapter.name: reference_suffix
adapter.description: The string that is included after each reference (for multiple-choice questions).

adapter.name: chain_of_thought_prefix
adapter.description: The string that is included before each chain of thought. (e.g., 'Let's think step by step')

adapter.name: chain_of_thought_suffix
adapter.description: The string that is included after each chain of thought. (e.g., 'The correct answer is')

adapter.name: output_prefix
adapter.description: The string that is included before the correct answer/predicted output (e.g., 'Answer:').

adapter.name: output_suffix
adapter.description: The string that is included after the correct answer/predicted output (e.g., '\n').

adapter.name: instance_prefix
adapter.description: The string that is included before each instance (e.g., '\n\n').

adapter.name: substitutions
adapter.description: A list of regular expression substitutions (e.g., replacing '\n' with ';\n') to perform at the very end on the prompt.

adapter.name: max_train_instances
adapter.description: Maximum number of training instances to include in the prompt (currently by randomly sampling).

adapter.name: max_eval_instances
adapter.description: Maximum number of instances to evaluate on (over all splits - test, valid, etc.).

adapter.name: num_outputs
adapter.description: Maximum number of possible outputs to generate by sampling multiple outputs.

adapter.name: num_train_trials
adapter.description: Number of trials, where in each trial we choose an independent, random set of training instances. Used to compute variance.

adapter.name: num_trials
adapter.description: Number of trials, where we query the model with the same requests, but different random seeds.

adapter.name: sample_train
adapter.description: If true, randomly sample N training examples; if false, select N consecutive training examples

adapter.name: model_deployment
adapter.description: Name of the language model deployment (<host_organization>/<model name>) to send requests to.

adapter.name: model
adapter.description: Name of the language model (<creator_organization>/<model name>) to send requests to.

adapter.name: temperature
adapter.description: Temperature parameter used in generation.

adapter.name: max_tokens
adapter.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate.

adapter.name: stop_sequences
adapter.description: List of stop sequences. Output generation will be stopped if any stop sequence is encountered.

adapter.name: random
adapter.description: Random seed (string), which guarantees reproducibility.

adapter.name: multi_label
adapter.description: If true, for instances with multiple correct reference, the gold answer should be considered to be all of the correct references rather than any of the correct references.

adapter.name: image_generation_parameters
adapter.description: Parameters for image generation.

adapter.name: eval_splits
adapter.description: The splits from which evaluation instances will be drawn.

models.name: ai21/jamba-instruct
models.description: Jamba Instruct is an instruction tuned version of Jamba, which uses a hybrid Transformer-Mamba mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture that interleaves blocks of Transformer and Mamba layers. ([blog](https://www.ai21.com/blog/announcing-jamba-instruct))

models.name: ai21/jamba-1.5-mini
models.description: Jamba 1.5 Mini is a long-context, hybrid SSM-Transformer instruction following foundation model that is optimized for function calling, structured output, and grounded generation. ([blog](https://www.ai21.com/blog/announcing-jamba-model-family))

models.name: ai21/jamba-1.5-large
models.description: Jamba 1.5 Large is a long-context, hybrid SSM-Transformer instruction following foundation model that is optimized for function calling, structured output, and grounded generation. ([blog](https://www.ai21.com/blog/announcing-jamba-model-family))

models.name: amazon/nova-lite-v1:0
models.description: Amazon Nova Lite Model

models.name: amazon/nova-micro-v1:0
models.description: Amazon Nova Micro Model

models.name: anthropic/claude-instant-1.2
models.description: A lightweight version of Claude, a model trained using reinforcement learning from human feedback ([docs](https://www.anthropic.com/index/introducing-claude)).

models.name: anthropic/claude-2.1
models.description: Claude 2.1 is a general purpose large language model developed by Anthropic. It uses a transformer architecture and is trained via unsupervised learning, RLHF, and Constitutional AI (including both a supervised and Reinforcement Learning (RL) phase). ([model card](https://efficient-manatee.files.svdcdn.com/production/images/Model-Card-Claude-2.pdf))

models.name: anthropic/claude-3-haiku-20240307
models.description: Claude 3 is a a family of models that possess vision and multilingual capabilities. They were trained with various methods such as unsupervised learning and Constitutional AI ([blog](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-family)).

models.name: anthropic/claude-3-sonnet-20240229
models.description: Claude 3 is a a family of models that possess vision and multilingual capabilities. They were trained with various methods such as unsupervised learning and Constitutional AI ([blog](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-family)).

models.name: anthropic/claude-3-opus-20240229
models.description: Claude 3 is a a family of models that possess vision and multilingual capabilities. They were trained with various methods such as unsupervised learning and Constitutional AI ([blog](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-family)).

models.name: anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-20241022
models.description: Claude 3.5 Haiku is a Claude 3 family model which matches the performance of Claude 3 Opus at a similar speed to the previous generation of Haiku ([blog](https://www.anthropic.com/news/3-5-models-and-computer-use)).

models.name: anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620
models.description: Claude 3.5 Sonnet is a Claude 3 family model which outperforms Claude 3 Opus while operating faster and at a lower cost. ([blog](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet))

models.name: anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
models.description: Claude 3.5 Sonnet is a Claude 3 family model which outperforms Claude 3 Opus while operating faster and at a lower cost ([blog](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet)). This is an upgraded snapshot released on 2024-10-22 ([blog](https://www.anthropic.com/news/3-5-models-and-computer-use)).

models.name: cohere/command-r
models.description: Command R is a multilingual 35B parameter model with a context length of 128K that has been trained with conversational tool use capabilities.

models.name: cohere/command-r-plus
models.description: Command R+ is a multilingual 104B parameter model with a context length of 128K that has been trained with conversational tool use capabilities.

models.name: databricks/dbrx-instruct
models.description: DBRX is a large language model with a fine-grained mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture that uses 16 experts and chooses 4. It has 132B total parameters, of which 36B parameters are active on any input. ([blog post](https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-dbrx-new-state-art-open-llm))

models.name: deepseek-ai/deepseek-llm-67b-chat
models.description: DeepSeek LLM Chat is a open-source language model trained on 2 trillion tokens in both English and Chinese, and fine-tuned supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02954))

models.name: deepseek-ai/deepseek-v3
models.description: DeepSeek v3 a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 671B total parameters with 37B activated for each token. It adopts Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE architectures. ([paper](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3/blob/main/DeepSeek_V3.pdf))
